title: Question tags (It's nice, isn't it?)
short: El «¿verdad?» del inglés: copia el auxiliar y le da la vuelta. It's lovely, ==isn't it==? You don't smoke, ==do you==?

story.title: El «¿verdad?» inglés
story.text: En español añadimos «¿verdad?» o «¿no?». En inglés esa coletilla ==cambia== según la frase: se llama ==question tag==.

examples.t: It's a lovely day, isn't it?

story.title: Al revés
story.text: Frase ==afirmativa== → coletilla ==negativa==. Frase ==negativa== → coletilla ==afirmativa==. Y siempre con ==pronombre==: she, he, it, they.

examples.t: Your sister is a nurse, isn't she?

story.title: Copia el auxiliar
story.text: Mira el verbo auxiliar de la frase y repítelo en la coletilla.

story.title: ¿Sin auxiliar? Do, does, did
story.text: Si el verbo va solo (presente o pasado simple), la coletilla usa ==do / does / did==.

examples.t: Your friend lives in London, doesn't he?
You liked the film, didn't you?

story.title: Español fijo, inglés variable
story.text: «¿Verdad?» y «¿no?» no cambian nunca. En inglés la coletilla ==copia== el auxiliar y el sujeto. Por eso ==isn't it?== no vale para todo.

story.title: Errores típicos
story.text:
❌ You like dancing, isn't it? ✅ You like dancing, ==don't you==?
❌ Your mum is a teacher, isn't it? ✅ …, ==isn't she==?
❌ She went, doesn't she? ✅ She went, ==didn't== she?

story.title: La entonación lo cambia todo
story.text: Si la voz ==baja== ↘, solo confirmas algo que ya sabes. Si ==sube== ↗, preguntas de verdad porque no estás segura.

compare.es: En español la coletilla es siempre la misma: «¿verdad?», «¿no?», «¿a que sí?». No depende del verbo ni de la persona.
compare.target: En inglés la coletilla (question tag) se construye con el auxiliar de la frase y un pronombre, y lleva la polaridad contraria: afirmativa → negativa (It's cold, isn't it?), negativa → afirmativa (You aren't cold, are you?). Si no hay auxiliar, se usa do/does/did. Con I am, la coletilla es aren't I?

errors.why: La coletilla copia el verbo: like → don't you.

errors.wrong: Your daughter is a nurse, isn't it?
errors.right: Your daughter is a nurse, isn't she?
errors.why: Hablamos de tu hija: she, no it.

errors.wrong: Your brother went to Paris, doesn't he?
errors.right: Your brother went to Paris, didn't he?

errors.why: Con I am, la coletilla es aren't I? Es una excepción.

exercises.why: Afirmativa con is → coletilla negativa: isn't it?
Lives no tiene auxiliar: con he, doesn't.
They've got = they have got: se copia have.
Won't es negativo → coletilla afirmativa: will he?

exercises.q: I'm a bit too old for this, ___?
exercises.why: Con I am, la coletilla es aren't I? (excepción).

exercises.q: Your friends weren't at the party, ___?

exercises.why: Se copia should, en negativa: shouldn't we?
Love sin auxiliar, con you: don't.

exercises.q: Your son hasn't called yet, ___ he?
exercises.es: Tu hijo todavía no ha llamado, ¿no?

exercises.q: The film was really sad, ___ it?
Your sister doesn't eat meat, ___ she?
You'll help me with the cake, ___ you?
Your grandson can swim now, ___ he?
exercises.why: Se copia can en negativa: can't he?

answer: Your husband works too much, doesn't he?
The children were very tired, weren't they?
exercises.why: Were → weren't, y the children → they.

answer: You haven't seen my glasses, have you?
We met last summer, didn't we?
exercises.why: Met es pasado simple → didn't we?

exercises.q: Your daughter is a nurse, isn't it?
exercises.why: Hablamos de tu hija: isn't she?
Like no lleva be: la coletilla es don't you?

exercises.q: Your mum is not well, isn't she?
exercises.why: La frase es negativa (is not) → coletilla afirmativa: is she?

exercises.q: They live near the beach, aren't they?
Your brother went to Paris, doesn't he?

exercises.answer: Your friend lives in London doesn't he

answer: You are not angry, are you?
It was a beautiful wedding, wasn't it?
It was a lovely wedding, wasn't it?

exercises.q: You've met my grandson, haven't you?

exercises.context: Sabes que tu amiga ha estado en Escocia; solo quieres confirmarlo y seguir charlando.
options: You've been to Scotland, haven't you? (la voz baja ↘)
You've been to Scotland, haven't you? (la voz sube ↗)
exercises.answer: You've been to Scotland, haven't you? (la voz baja ↘)
exercises.why: Si ya lo sabes y solo confirmas, la entonación baja.

exercises.context: No estás segura de la hora del tren y se lo preguntas de verdad a tu marido.
options: The train leaves at ten, doesn't it? (la voz sube ↗)
The train leaves at ten, doesn't it? (la voz baja ↘)
exercises.answer: The train leaves at ten, doesn't it? (la voz sube ↗)
exercises.why: Cuando dudas y preguntas de verdad, la entonación sube.
Con Let's…, la coletilla es shall we?
